note: A signed test run for the receiver gate. The keys below are test keys, made for this file and discarded when it was written: they sign nothing outside this file. The refusal reasons are measured, not asserted — scripts/agent-example-check.mjs re-runs the gate over every case and fails if the answer changes.
keyring_note: kid -> Ed25519 public key, base64 SPKI. A receiver builds its keyring from the server environment, never from the browser. The fingerprint is the SHA-256 of this object with its keys in sorted order; a receiver prints it so an operator can confirm the keyring it trusts is the keyring of the file a stranger downloaded.

refusals.why: the request carries no authority
the mandate's not_after is in the past
the decision verdict is deny
the request's args do not match the proposal's args_digest
the mandate permits transfer, the request asks for withdraw

refusals.case: the decision key is the acting key
refusals.why: the same key signed the decision and would sign the action

refusals.case: the mandate key signed the decision
refusals.why: the key that granted the authority also granted itself permission
the proposal's mid does not match the mandate it travels with
the decision's pid does not match the proposal it travels with
the last characters of the decision signature were changed
the decision names a kid that is not in the keyring
the decision names an algorithm this receiver does not check
the settlement is 250.00 and the mandate caps spending at 100.00

refusals.case: currency the mandate does not permit
refusals.why: the settlement is in USD and the mandate permits AUD only
the decision said deny and the envelope still names an action
the mandate allows one action and one is already on the chain
the same proposal was accepted once already
refusals.note: first post allowed=true, second post allowed=false

payment.note: One permitted payment and the refusals a payment door must make. The gate proves the permission was signed; the door's own rules apply the mandate's spend limit and currency to the amount about to be charged, because a limit belongs to the mandate and cannot be read out of a request. The price ids below are placeholders: a live door uses its own price ids from the server environment.

refusals.why: the request carries no authority to spend

refusals.case: the same payment proposal posted twice
refusals.why: one proposal buys one payment

refusals.case: a payment with a forged signature
refusals.why: the last characters of the decision signature were changed

refusals.case: a tier the door does not sell
refusals.why: the price list is the server's, and this tier is not on it

refusals.case: an amount above the mandate limit
refusals.why: the mandate caps spending at 11.00 and this asks for 20000.00

refusals.case: a currency the mandate does not permit
refusals.why: the mandate permits AUD and the price list sells USD

refusals.case: a payment made through another tool
refusals.why: a permission for one tool is not a permission for the payment door

settled_run.note: The same contract after the action ran: one action record on the chain and a settlement bound to the decision. This is what the breach pack and the settlement path verify.

how_to_check: npm run build && npm run check:example — re-runs the gate over every case in this file and fails if an answer changes
POST the `request` object of any refusal case to the receiver: the answer must be refused with the stated reason
The `allow` case must be permitted; the `settled_run` package must verify clean with the keyring above

The `payment.allow` request must be permitted by the gate and by the payment rules; each `payment.refusals` entry carries `checked_by`: `gate` means the gate refuses it, `door` means the gate permits it and the door's money rules refuse it
The case marked `post_twice` must be posted twice: the first post is permitted, the second is refused as `replay`
